name: Inside Out
label: Revelation
lede: One seven-inch, fewer than three years, a final show in Long Beach, and a song title from the record they never made that ended up on the side of a band that filled stadiums.

eras.title: The side project that stopped being one
eras.text: Inside Out started as a sideline for two guitarists in the Orange County band Hard Stance. It took a drummer's push and a new guitar player to turn it into the band Zack de la Rocha actually sang in, pulling from Minor Threat, Bad Brains, Dag Nasty and, as the songs got heavier, Led Zeppelin.

years.h: Two [[Hard Stance|3029fc29-bf7c-4f78-8bfc-97c0bf144c6d]] guitarists try something on the side
years.p: [[Zack de la Rocha|aa659468-db56-41c9-b6fe-61f4bb2ef1a6]] and Rob Haworth both play guitar in Hard Stance. Inside Out is their extra band, with Zack out front on vocals.

q: There was something really sincere in his eyes when he was singing.
years.p: They start at the bottom of a bill in the fall. Alex Barreto, Hard Stance's drummer, joins and is the one who talks Zack into taking Inside Out seriously.
years.xp: Barreto saw the singer before most people did. Zack had been a guitarist in Hard Stance, and Inside Out was the first band where he stood at the mic.

years.p: DiCara, fresh from New York's Beyond, replaces Rob Haworth and the sound opens up. As DiCara put it later, they took a little of everything they liked instead of copying one subgenre.

years.h: A new rhythm section for the studio
years.p: Mark Haworth, Rob's brother and another Hard Stance alum, takes bass. [[Chris Bratton|cbaf85ca-1bc7-4eb0-b9cb-ca5d8773b27f]], of [[No for an Answer|23d26104-95e2-473f-a704-ab0bcd702da3]] and [[Chain of Strength|81a3c11e-ac20-4bb4-8614-06b157e802d8]], replaces Barreto on drums before the sessions.

eras.title: Four songs Revelation can't keep in the racks
eras.text: One record, one East Coast trip, one radio session. That's the whole official output, and it's been enough for Revelation to call it possibly the most popular release the label has ever put out.

years.h: East with [[Shelter|d5157104-76b1-4b8b-90c2-9ff994f940db]] and [[Quicksand|3c9f8bef-a658-4204-9ee8-7e95d2535b32]], in a van that dies on day one
years.p: The one East Coast run: a June package out of New York with Ray Cappo's Shelter and the brand-new Quicksand, through Buffalo, Cleveland and City Gardens in New Jersey. The van's engine seized the first day and Revelation's Jordan Cooper paid to fix it. On June 28 they play the Unisound in Reading, PA; a VHS of that set surfaces 26 years later.
years.xp: The roadie crew included former Beyond singer Kevin Egan and a young [[Derrick Green|eb624b5f-6580-42d4-af83-19fad8e866ab]], years before he fronted [[Sepultura|1d93c839-22e7-4f76-ad84-d27039efc048]]. Egan later wrote the tour up for No Echo, clean-sock shortage and all.

years.p: Four songs on the original seven-inch, six on the later CD. Revelation calls it possibly its most popular release ever, and praises a vocal performance as intense as anything on a hardcore record.
years.xp:
Twenty years later an Orange County record store manager told OC Weekly it still sold once or twice a week, and they never let it go out of stock.

The record kept doing its work on bands that came later: Wikipedia lists [[Refused|42884e27-dfb8-453d-990f-2ffd90bc2d1a]], [[Have Heart|e519e012-e1a3-4592-b3f6-5a16227ab654]], [[Turnstile|7b748dac-f5ce-45a7-9b95-c1d8b5b013ed]] and even [[Linkin Park|f59c5520-5f46-4d2c-b2c4-822eabf53419]] among those who drew from it.

years.p: A session on the Loyola Marymount college station captures unreleased songs at broadcast quality, the best-sounding record of the material that came after the EP.

eras.title: A monk, a last show, and a band name
eras.text: The guitarist's turn to Krishna consciousness ended the band. What was left behind was a finished set of new songs, including one with a title that would be famous by the end of the next year.

years.p: Shortly after the EP, DiCara joins [[Ray Cappo|e8357f9d-f7f5-4858-a766-aef004bb38a6]]'s Krishna-conscious [[Shelter|d5157104-76b1-4b8b-90c2-9ff994f940db]], becomes a Hare Krishna monk, and later starts [[108|7f0c252a-bd45-4fe0-b306-478eeb07b97b]].
The final set includes songs meant for a second record, among them Darkness of Greed and one called Rage Against the Machine. A clean remaster of the tape turns up in 2013.

years.big: Inside Out's next record was going to be called Rage Against the Machine
years.h: The second album's title walks off with the singer
years.p: The band is done by the fall. Zack takes the unused title with him to Los Angeles, where [[Tom Morello|42a636a0-dbe4-4d0c-abe2-1590fad9531b]], [[Tim Commerford|4d61abe3-ce6d-4383-b2cd-8b4491496549]] and [[Brad Wilk|b48aebac-8c3e-48aa-b5e6-2b38f30f5f78]] become [[Rage Against the Machine|3798b104-01cb-484c-a3b0-56adc6399b80]]. Haworth goes to State of the Nation, Barreto to Statue.
years.xp:
The planned follow-up to No Spiritual Surrender had a working title, Rage Against the Machine, and a song to match. Neither came out under the Inside Out name.

Within a year it was the name of a band signed to Epic.

eras.title: The tape-trader's band
eras.text: With one official record, Inside Out's afterlife has run on bootlegs, surfacing tapes and younger bands. Every few years another piece of the story shows up.

years.p: Oktopus of Dälek turns the title track into Ghost in the Machine for the mashup album Threat: Music That Inspired the Movie.
OC Weekly checks in twenty years on: the EP moves once or twice a week at a local shop, and the store reorders whenever it runs out.

years.h: The last show, finally in good sound
years.p: A high-quality remaster of the May 18, 1991 Long Beach set surfaces, with the never-released Rage Against the Machine and Darkness of Greed.
VHS footage of the June 28, 1990 show in Pennsylvania appears online.
Bandcamp Daily marks the anniversary with Tony Rettman's oral history. Barreto's summary: Inside Out had something special, rehearsing or on stage.
The band's Instagram posts Sacrifice with that question, and the news sites run with it. The line-up question was never publicly answered.
For the Live Lounge, the Baltimore band covers Inside Out, with Brendan Yates channeling Zack. A thirty-five-year-old song from a band with one EP, on national radio in Britain.
